title: Lamine Yamal's family struggles shaped his inspiring World Cup journey
description: Lamine Yamal's rise to winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup is inseparable from the story of the family that built him. His mother Sheila Ebana was 16 when she gave birth to him. His father Mounir, a Moroccan immigrant, worked construction and street jobs to stay afloat. His grandmother Fátima crossed from Morocco to Spain alone, undocumented, and worked three jobs to bring her children over. His father survived a life-threatening stabbing in August 2024. Yamal's name itself honours two strangers who helped his parents financially before he was born. This is the full human story behind the boy who hugged his little brother on a World Cup pitch in New Jersey.

The Kansas City Current co-owner reflected on why she wants her children to see women in leadership as the norm after helping build one of the biggest success stories in women's sports. Here's what Brittany said during her speech, why she was honored, Patrick Mahomes' loving reaction, and how her impact continues to shape opportunities for women on and off the field
